title: New Poll: Arab Americans Are Leaving the Republican Party and Have Surprising 2028 Favorites

While the commentariat often talk _about_ Arab Americans, seldom do we hear
_from_ them. But we should. A [new national
poll](https://www.aaiusa.org/library/arab-american-vote-2026) of Arab
Americans has been shared exclusively with **Zeteo**. The findings are
fascinating, from whom Arab Americans support in 2028 (on both sides of the
aisle), to how many identify as socialists or MAGA Republicans, to how
consequential Israel and Gaza will be to their votes.

Commissioned by the Arab American Institute and conducted by John Zogby
Strategies, the poll surveyed Arab Americans nationwide ahead of the 2026
midterms and as the 2028 presidential election looms.

For years, media depictions of Arab American opinion have been at best mixed,
at worst, often condescending or racist. Some such media treatment came in
response to the Washington establishment's disdain for those who stand against
the bipartisan machine fueling Israel's genocide in Gaza - with Arab Americans
percevied as the primary source of inconvenient dissent (a proposition proved
wrong [time](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/kamala-harris-gaza-israel-biden-
election-poll) and [again](https://zeteo.com/p/poll-harris-democrats-gaza-
ceasefire-arms-embargo)).

While corporate media has dismissed Arab Americans and many other groups when
it comes to Israel and Palestine, the importance of the issue has not gone
away. A whopping 90% of respondents to the new poll said the crisis in Gaza
would be very or somewhat important in determining their vote in 2028.

A plurality, 41%, said they would not support a candidate who refused to end
unconditional support for Israel, including 56% of respondents aged 18-29 and
46% of women.

As far as the 2028 primaries go, two candidates in each party stood above the
rest.

On the Democratic side, voters were split between Kamala Harris (30%) and
Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (29%), with Gavin Newsom on 18% and Ro Khanna, Josh
Shapiro, and Pete Buttigieg trailing in single digits.

On the Republican side of the aisle, Donald Trump Jr. led the field at 30%,
with Vice President JD Vance at 25%. Marco Rubio and Ted Cruz trailed at 8%
each, and Ron DeSantis rounded out the field at 6%.

"In 2026, the unpopularity of the Trump administration and the Democratic
Party's movement away from unquestioned support for Israel have undone much of
the damage the Biden administration caused to Arab American support in the
2024 election," the Arab American Institute writes.

Still, the poll finds Arab Americans who identify as independents at a
historic 31% - following [national](https://news.gallup.com/poll/700499/new-
high-identify-political-independents.aspx) trends rejecting the two-party
system. Nevertheless, respondents who identified as Democrats bounced back
after a sharp decline during the past two administrations.

While a staying portion of Arab Americans identify as Republicans, when it
comes to political ideology, the findings are a bit more nuanced. More
respondents, for example, identified as democratic socialists than as MAGA
Republicans and conservatives combined.

"There's a convergence of views on critical issues, and Trump's on the wrong
side of every one of them," James Zogby, managing director of Zogby Research
Services, tells **Zeteo**. "This is a Democratic year for the community, and
it's a return to where they were in 2020. Now, where will they be in 2028? It
depends, as they say, on the candidates' views."

Of those who identified as Democrats, a plurality (39%) identified as
democratic socialists - more than any other ideological group.

When it comes to voting, 59% of respondents said they planned to vote for the
Democratic candidate in their district, compared to just 26% who said they'd
be voting for the Republican.

Unfortunately, 65% of Arab Americans reported experiencing discrimination due
to their ethnicity or country of origin - the fourth conservative survey in
which that figure has increased. Nearly three out of four respondents aged
18-29 report facing discrimination.

"Arab Americans are like the rest of us. In some ways, they're the canary in
the coal mine," Zogby says. "When Israel was running roughshod over
Palestinians, and people were beginning to get upset about not just about
Gaza, but about the role that [pro-Israel lobby group] AIPAC plays [in U.S.
politics], Arab Americans were given a warning…and people didn't pay
attention. And now what they're saying is this appeal to bigotry, the ruinous
nature of the policies on the economy, and dividing people - they're saying
'Enough's enough, and we're rejecting it,' and so in many ways, this is a
community that is pretty much where the country is."
